questions.question: What is the primary job of a KEM like ML-KEM?
options: Encrypt arbitrary-length messages to a recipient
Establish a shared secret key over a public channel
Sign messages so recipients can verify authenticity
Generate random numbers faster than a CSPRNG
questions.explanation: A KEM’s API is KeyGen/Encaps/Decaps to agree on a shared secret; bulk data encryption is done with symmetric AEAD.

questions.question: In one sentence, what does IND-CCA security protect against?
options: Attackers who can request signatures on chosen messages
Attackers who can ask for decryptions of chosen ciphertexts (with a challenge restriction)
Attackers who can observe only public keys and ciphertexts but never interact
Attackers who can factor large integers efficiently
questions.explanation: IND-CCA models an attacker who can adaptively query a decryption oracle on chosen ciphertexts (except for the challenge ciphertext).

questions.question: Why does Kyber-style polynomial multiplication in R_q = Z_q[X]/(X^N + 1) include a sign flip on wrap-around terms?
options: Because X^N is treated as 0 in this ring
Because X^N is treated as 1 in this ring
Because X^N is treated as -1 in this ring
Because coefficients are stored in two’s-complement form
questions.explanation: In the quotient by (X^N + 1), we have X^N ≡ -1, so terms that wrap past degree N-1 pick up a minus sign.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Compress/Decompress in ML-KEM-style schemes?
options: Reduce ciphertext size by mapping mod-q coefficients to fewer bits with controlled error
Make the encryption deterministic so randomness is unnecessary
Prevent side-channel attacks by forcing constant-time division
Turn a KEM into a signature scheme
questions.explanation: Compression is a lossy scaling from Z_q to d-bit integers; decryption still works because noise + rounding loss stays below the decision threshold.

questions.question: In K-PKE.Encrypt, why is A transposed (using A^T) when computing u?
options: It removes the need for any hashing
It matches the algebra so decryption can compute v - s^T u and cancel the main term
It makes ciphertexts shorter by a factor of k
It ensures all coefficients are already compressed
questions.explanation: Using A^T aligns the terms so decryption’s dot product with s cancels the shared A·s·r structure, leaving (mostly) the message plus bounded noise.

questions.question: What is the point of the re-encryption check in ML-KEM decapsulation (the FO-style check)?
options: To verify that the ciphertext is well-formed without revealing a decryption-validity oracle
To speed up polynomial multiplication by caching intermediate products
To convert the KEM into a deterministic signature primitive
To allow encrypting arbitrary messages instead of random ones
questions.explanation: The check prevents chosen-ciphertext attacks by ensuring decapsulation only uses the decrypted value if it reproduces the ciphertext under deterministic re-encryption.

questions.question: In implicit rejection, what does decapsulation output when the ciphertext check fails?
options: A fixed all-zero key so callers can detect failure
A pseudorandom-looking shared secret derived from a secret fallback value and the ciphertext
The decrypted message so callers can debug mismatches
The public key so the caller can retry encapsulation
questions.explanation: Implicit rejection avoids exposing validity: the output stays computationally indistinguishable from a real shared secret even for malformed ciphertexts.

questions.question: Attack-themed: What goes wrong if your decapsulation path leaks whether the ciphertext check passed (e.g., via logs or timing)?
options: An attacker can turn it into a chosen-ciphertext oracle and extract information about secrets over many queries
An attacker can factor q and recover the secret key immediately
An attacker can forge signatures because KEMs and signatures are interchangeable
Nothing important; it only affects performance, not security
questions.explanation: Any observable validity signal can enable adaptive chosen-ciphertext strategies (and often side-channel amplification), which the FO transform is designed to prevent.
